s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic, progressive, itchy skin lesions with erosions and scarring
salient_findings: Multiple itchy erythematous to violaceous papules and plaques on the left shin
Milia and erosions with partially detached epidermis
key_facts: Female patient in her 30s
Symptoms present for more than 10 years
Lesions localized to the left shin
No abnormalities of the mucous membranes, nails, hair, or teeth
No extracutaneous involvement
Histopathologic examination revealed dermoepidermal separation
Multiple milia in the superficial dermis
Novel heterozygous missense variant in COL7A1 gene
Pruritic erythematous to violaceous lichenified papules and plaques

differentials: Inherited epidermolysis bullosa with pyloric atresia
Epidermolysis bullosa simplex with mottled pigmentation
per_call: Inherited epidermolysis bullosa with pyloric atresia
Epidermolysis bullosa simplex with mottled pigmentation

shortlist.label: Epidermolysis bullosa pruriginosa
shortlist.why_kept: Matches clinical presentation of itchy, violaceous papules and plaques with erosions and scarring, and histopathologic findings of dermoepidermal separation and milia

shortlist.label: Dominant dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with the novel heterozygous missense variant in COL7A1 gene and the presence of pruritic skin lesions

shortlist.label: Dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa
shortlist.why_kept: Shares similar clinical and histopathologic features with the case, including dermoepidermal separation and milia

shortlist.label: Bullous pemphigoid
shortlist.why_kept: Could be considered due to the presence of pruritic, erythematous lesions and histopathologic findings of dermoepidermal separation

shortlist.label: Lichen simplex chronicus
shortlist.why_kept: Possible diagnosis given the chronic, progressive nature of the skin lesions and the presence of lichenification

raw.rationale: The presence of pruritic erythematous to violaceous lichenified papules and plaques, dermoepidermal separation, and milia in the superficial dermis, along with a novel heterozygous missense variant in the COL7A1 gene, are consistent with epidermolysis bullosa pruriginosa (EBP), a subtype of dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa characterized by intense pruritus and lichenification.

rejected.label: Dominant dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa
rejected.why: While the COL7A1 gene mutation is consistent with dominant dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa, the specific clinical presentation and localization of lesions are more characteristic of EBP.

rejected.label: Dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa
rejected.why: This is a broader category that includes EBP, but the specific features of pruritus and lichenification point more specifically to EBP.

rejected.label: Bullous pemphigoid
rejected.why: The absence of mucous membrane involvement and the specific histopathologic findings are not typical of bullous pemphigoid.

rejected.label: Lichen simplex chronicus
rejected.why: While lichenification is present, the underlying dermoepidermal separation and COL7A1 gene mutation indicate a more complex condition than lichen simplex chronicus.
